headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 3 studies yielded an effect size of 0.84 (95% CI: 0.68–1.04), indicating no statistically significant association between Vitamin B2 and renal cell carcinoma. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by low heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.

effect_size.excerpt: When the cutoff for serum folate was moved by 10% from 6.6 nmol/L down to 5.9 nmol/L or up to 7.3 nmol/L, the odds ratios were 1.66 (0.98-2.80) and 1.16 (0.76-1.78), respectively. Cut-points above 6.8 nmol/L consistently yielded lower odds ratios, suggesting that the increased risk applies only to the lowest concentrations of serum folate.
